gap: No result ChatGPT got states cost per usable Wh or Wh per lb. Worked out from the sellers' own figures, the Bixpower LF1220 20Ah battery with its 6 A charger comes to $0.66/Wh and 45.7 Wh/lb. The Dakota Lithium Powerbox 10 comes to $1.66/Wh and 30 Wh/lb. Both charge from empty in about 3.3 h on their included chargers.
standout_why: I compared against the result pages ChatGPT got: TackleDirect, InvertersRUs and TotalBattery for the Powerbox 10, plus Bixpower's LF1220 and LF1220 + 60 W solar pages. ChatGPT cited none of them. Each page gives raw inputs only: price, Ah, weight and charger amps. Neither the Dakota pages nor the Bixpower pages put cost per Wh, Wh per lb or charge time from the included charger side by side. The Dakota pages also give no Wh figure and no charge time for the included 3 A charger, only solar times. Nobody has noticed that Dakota's solar claim assumes a 20 W panel delivers 67–86% of its rated output, while Bixpower plans for 42%.
decides: For a small 12 V battery with a charger in the box, this points to the Bixpower LF1220 (20Ah) over the Dakota Lithium Powerbox 10. It has about 2.1× the energy (256 Wh vs 120 Wh) for $29 less ($169.95 vs $199), and charges in the same time (20 Ah ÷ 6 A = 3.3 h; 10 Ah ÷ 3 A = 3.3 h). The Powerbox 10's case with USB and 12 V outlets is the only reason to pay its $1.66/Wh. The 100Ah kits on our page (Redodo, Power Queen, ECO-WORTHY) could not be priced today, so this finding doesn't settle the 100Ah pick.

findings.note: Page claim: one 20 W panel fully charges it in 7–9 h. 120 Wh ÷ 9 h = 13.3 W; 120 Wh ÷ 7 h = 17.1 W. By comparison, Bixpower plans for 42% of rated output.
